headline: Alignment and search tools revise scoring for tandem repeats, proteins and DNA barcodes
label: Sequence Alignment And Search Tools
summary: Recent late-December 2025 preprints refine alignment and search scoring for repeats, protein families, barcoding, and long-read assembly.
synthesis: The dominant thread is departure from fixed scoring or comparison schemes in alignment and search. NW-flex retains the Needleman-Wunsch/Gotoh recurrence but adds an internal flexible block that can contract, aimed at reads from short tandem repeats. BABAPPAlign replaces static substitution matrices with a learned residue-level neural scoring function built on protein language model embeddings, within a multiple sequence alignment engine. TGAO removes user-set parameters from DNA barcoding by combining reference tiling, gap-robust syncmer sketching and approximate nearest-neighbor search. RefLA is less directly a scoring revision: it is a reference-assisted long-read assembler that uses alignment-guided structural refinement and localized reassembly. What is new across the scoring-focused items is greater flexibility or learned information in how sequences are compared. The items differ in task and maturity, and all four are preprints.
